prize_parts.citation: For chemically induced proximity that directs proteins to the ubiquitin-proteasome system for degradation, through heterobifunctional PROTACs and the identification of cereblon as the target of molecular-glue degraders

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B019 with Crews, Deshaies and Handa. After round 1 the case rests on one claim that I can test as an experimentalist. Both strands, the PROTAC and the cereblon glue, work by the same chemical act, a small molecule that makes an E3 ligase act on a protein it would not otherwise ubiquitinate. That act is defined at the level of ternary-complex structures and degradation kinetics, and it has been reproduced independently across many targets and laboratories. Crews and Deshaies supply the designed, heterobifunctional version. Handa supplies the molecular explanation of how thalidomide-type drugs work, which turned a decades-old clinical puzzle into a defined mechanism. I want a prize to stand on a measurement-backed mechanism and not on a projected clinical outcome, and this one does. It also remains the only ballot with explicit support from five of eight members, and I give that weight only as a sign that the scientific case survived scrutiny from very different fields, not as a substitute for the case itself.
statement.case_against: The credit is crowded and any three-name cut will look arbitrary to some. Ciulli, Sakamoto, Gray, Ito and Kim made real contributions, and Ciulli's VHL ligands and structural work are what made PROTACs drug-like. The two strands have different histories, and a single citation covering both is a drafting risk. No degrader is approved, to my knowledge, and I have not verified that from the files. The first PROTAC used a peptide ligand with poor permeability, so the early demonstrations were proof of concept. Finally, the ternary-complex cooperativity that Linke and Sparr point to is only partly quantified, and as someone who measures things I do not dismiss that.

responses.point: Somfai asks what is chemically new in degraders, says the PROTAC and cereblon glue stories should not be merged without a clear reason, and holds B034 (Buchwald, Hartwig) first on three decades of confirmation.
responses.response: You give the reason to merge in your own question about what is new. It is not a new reaction, it is a new way to make an existing enzyme catalyse a reaction on a chosen substrate. The PROTAC and cereblon routes both do this and differ only in whether the proximity is designed or found. That is why I keep both strands and name the shared mechanism in the citation. I agree that two strands are a drafting risk, and the citation therefore has to name the E3-ligase principle and not just the products. On B034, I respect the replication record, but the 2010 cross-coupling prize covers the same catalytic cycle and the Kosugi and Migita precursor question is open, so I rank it behind B019 on novelty relative to prior recognition.

responses.point: Aqvist prefers Ciulli to Handa as the third name and a PROTAC-only citation, treating the glue arm as a competing credit stream and offering Handa as a possible second prize part.
responses.response: I take your argument that Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures are intrinsic to rational design, and I would not object if the committee chose that cut. I still prefer Handa. A second prize part is not available to me, since the cap of three unique names means Ciulli and Handa cannot both be credited if Crews and Deshaies stay. Without cereblon, the thalidomide-class degraders have no mechanism, and a PROTAC-only citation omits the one degrader class that has been in patients longest. The fact that we agree on Crews and Deshaies and the principle, and differ on one name, is a drafting question, not a doubt about the science.

responses.point: Linke, as chair, keeps maturity as a standing reservation on B019 because no approval is firm and ternary-complex cooperativity is only partly quantified, and still ranks nanopore sensing (B002) as a reasonable first choice.
responses.response: On the chair's question about evidence, I would accept as showing delivery that the mechanism is confirmed by structures and degradation kinetics in independent laboratories, and that several candidates have reached late-stage patient trials. I would not require a marketed degrader, because that makes the prize depend on a regulatory date. I do accept that the cooperativity biophysics is incomplete, but that is a reason the field is productive, not a reason to wait. On B002, I now list it as an alternative because the physical principle is clean and mature, and I think it is closer to chemistry than Somfai and Zou do. Attribution still blocks me: the Bayley step (engineered pores) cannot be put into a three-name cut that also holds Kasianowicz, Deamer and Akeson without leaving a decisive person out.

responses.point: Sparr prefers ionizable lipid nanoparticles (B045) because approved products and real-world data show maturity, and favours a PROTAC-only trio if B019 goes ahead.
responses.response: The lipid pKa and phase-behaviour chemistry is a real design principle, and approved products settle maturity. My difficulty is the same as yours: six credited names across Vancouver, Boston and industry, and a risk that the committee reads it as a second pandemic prize after Medicine 2023. On your request that the glue names be left out for coherence, I disagree. The coherence of B019 comes from the shared E3-ligase mechanism, and cereblon is the best-characterised molecular case of that mechanism. If the committee decides that B019 must wait for an approval, B045 would not be my fallback. I would turn to B043 first.

uncertainties: Whether Handa or Ciulli is the better third name; I weigh the cereblon mechanism of thalidomide above VHL ligand design, but I accept this is the most contestable seat on my ballot.
Whether one citation can honestly hold both the PROTAC and the molecular-glue strands, given that a prize can credit only three people in total.
Whether degraders will show durable clinical efficacy and safety by the time of recognition, and whether the committee will treat that as a condition.
Whether Handa's cereblon identification is independent enough of Ito and Sakamoto and of the earlier thalidomide work, and priority claims I cannot settle from the files.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. My work on nucleotide metabolism and genome stability at Umeå does not involve any shortlisted candidate, and I have no collaboration or institutional tie to any credited name. My field is scientifically adjacent to ubiquitin-dependent proteolysis only in the sense that both are cellular chemistry, which I do not regard as a conflict.
